answers.answer: stETH rewards accrue through rebases, so transfers alone miss quiet-period balance growth. A single midnight read would make the result fragile to one failed historical RPC read and would not preserve the bounded retry and wallet-allocation model. The accepted design establishes a launch-aligned baseline, samples each tracked wallet every 600 Ethereum blocks, and writes wallet-level daily rows. This captures rebasing yield with roughly two-hour observations while keeping the persisted read model daily. It avoids every-block replay cost, keeps earnings assigned to the wallet where they accrued, retries a failed launch baseline, and skips a later incomplete batch instead of writing partial daily actuals.

evidence.supports: Explains why event-only accounting fails and defines the sub-daily sampling plus daily persistence design.
Rejects transfer-only and every-block alternatives.
Defines wallet-level consumption and fail-closed or skip-batch behavior for unavailable reads.

answers.answer: The recurring garden creates one bounded issue because freshness signals do not prove semantic obsolescence, the full corpus is too large for careful review, and an unattended partial edit could remove operating knowledge. A deterministic, credential-free planner selects at most 10 documents or 15,000 source words. The scheduler creates at most one immutable live Agent Task issue and cannot edit repository content, open or merge a PR, deploy, or mutate production. A claimed or blocked packet retains its exact scope and blocks later packets. Semantic changes still require evidence, a claim, a normal reviewed PR, link repair, and catalog verification.

answers.answer: The read-only planner deterministically selects one lane per UTC week and advances shards after each six-lane cycle. Each packet contains at most 10 documents and 15,000 words; an empty lane produces no issue. The weekly workflow creates one fully specified Agent Task and stops. An `agent-ready` occurrence remains immutable until claimed. An `agent-active` or `in-pr` occurrence keeps its scope. A `needs-grooming` occurrence remains the single blocked packet until a human resolves or closes it. Duplicate markers or conflicting lifecycle labels fail closed for manual recovery. Before changing, demoting, or deleting a document, give it an evidence-backed disposition. Age alone is not evidence. Verify claims against owning code, workflows, provider contracts, or current canonical sources. Preserve ADR history, repair inbound links, and escalate conflicting authority. Semantic edits require a claimed issue and a normal reviewed PR. Finish with `pnpm docs:index --check`, regenerating and reviewing the catalog if classification changed.

evidence.supports: Defines deterministic weekly lane and shard selection plus packet bounds.
Defines the issue-only scheduler and claim boundary.
Defines behavior for ready, claimed, blocked, closed, duplicate, conflicting, and empty states.
Defines manual recovery for duplicate markers and lifecycle labels.
